This file is the INTERIM home so a contract is authorable without waiting on another team — the same correction §3a/W1 already took for the ref/resolver map: 'a registry row, authored once and later pushed upstream into _meta when the owning service catches up'. `_meta` WINS wherever a service supplies it, and `Completeness.source` records which one answered so an owner-published contract and one we wrote never merge into one indistinguishable row.

result_completeness._KNOWN_GAP: 🔴 THIS TOOL DOES NOT REPORT COMPLETENESS, and the contract records that rather than claiming a field that does not exist. Measured 2026-08-10: of 36 tools declaring paging, five never report it, and this is one of them — it returns at most `limit` rows with no is_complete, so a full page is indistinguishable from a truncated one.
result_completeness.runtime_compensation: CP-5.3 treats a page whose EXACT matches fill it as `truncated` and REFUSES rather than substituting, because 'exactly one match' is only true if the list was whole.
result_completeness.closes_when: glossary-service returns page{total,returned,is_complete}; the resolver then believes it and this gap entry is deleted.

compose_prose._why: The co-writer step the PO named as the point of the journey — CHAT-SERVICE'S OWN tool, and the row CP-5's exit was blocked on. It was underivable for weeks because it declared no `_meta` at all, so the essential set could name it and rung 2 could never admit it.

argument_supplier.instructions: model — what to write, or how to rewrite the source text. Only the caller knows this; there is no runtime value to fall back on.
argument_supplier.source_text: model — the existing text being transformed; omitted for fresh generation

repeat_semantics.signal_retained: 🔴 A repeat is NOT cost-removable here and must never be served from a cache: this tool calls a MODEL, so two identical calls legitimately return different prose, and answering the second from the first would silently replace a generation the author asked for. §3's rule cuts the other way for a generative tool — remove the SIGNAL of a loop, never the generation.

error_contract._why_retryable: Unlike every other member here, the failure mode is a model call: an upstream timeout is genuinely transient. Declared explicitly rather than defaulted, because C-7's fail-closed answer is `terminal_permanent` and this is the one tool where that would be wrong.

output_contract._verified_against: a RECORDED successful result in loreweave_chat, 2026-08-10 (session-level tool_calls). NOT read from the tool description — that method produced the wrong shape for 4 of the first 5 contracts authored.

glossary_propose_entity_edit._why: 🔴 THE LARGEST 0%-SUCCESS TOOL IN THE CORPUS — 101 calls / 12 sessions, every one refused. It is a CHAT-SERVICE FRONTEND tool whose NAME sits in glossary-service's namespace, so it was doubly invisible: absent from the federated snapshot, and misattributed by the name-prefix owner table. Admitting it is what lets it declare the members that address its own failure.

identifier_resolution.entity_id: an opaque id, NEVER a name and never a placeholder. Resolvable from a name via EntityRef (contracts/agent-runtime-ref-resolvers.json); the correct source is a prior `glossary_get_entity` or `glossary_search`.
identifier_resolution.book_id: an opaque id; the ambient book on a book-bound surface

argument_supplier.book_id: context — the runtime supplies the ambient book; not the model's to invent
argument_supplier.entity_id: model — but OBTAINED, not authored. 🔴 MEASURED 2026-08-10: 89 of the 101 recorded calls sent a model-invented placeholder (`placeholder_id_1` x60, `placeholder_id` x29, `new_entity_id_placeholder`). The value exists only in a prior read; there is nothing for the model to compose it from.
argument_supplier.base_version: model — obtained, not authored: the entity's `updated_at` from the same prior read, which is what makes the edit conflict-safe
argument_supplier.changes: model — the actual CONTENT of the edit, and the one argument here that genuinely is the model's

preconditions.unmet: refused before dispatch, naming how to obtain the scope
preconditions.requires_prior_read: 🔴 THE PRECONDITION THIS TOOL ACTUALLY FAILS ON, and it is not a scope: two of its four required arguments (`entity_id`, `base_version`) can only come from a prior `glossary_get_entity`. Its own description has said so since 2026-07-22 and the measured compliance is 0 of 101.

consent.mechanism: The turn SUSPENDS and the browser renders a diff card; the user Applies or dismisses. Nothing is written by calling this tool — which is why its tier is W and why a failure here costs a round trip rather than data.

effect_and_undo.effect: proposes an atomic multi-field edit to one existing entity; the write happens only on the user's Apply
effect_and_undo.undo: dismissing the card is the undo before the fact; after Apply, the entity's revision history (`glossary_list_entity_revisions` / `glossary_propose_restore_revision`) is the reversal path

partial_outcome.note: All `changes[]` apply TOGETHER or not at all — declared because the resume vocabulary (`applied_saved` / `applied_conflict` / `applied_error` / `dismissed`) has no per-change arm, so a partial result is not merely unwanted, it is unrepresentable.

repeat_semantics.signal_retained: 🔴 The measured shape is a LOOP on the same rejected arguments — 4 calls / 1 distinct args in a single turn appears in the corpus. The repeat is short-circuited before the wire and counted; the count is what escalates.

error_contract._measured: 🔴 ALL 101 recorded failures carry `result: null` and an `error` that is CHAT-SERVICE'S OWN VALIDATION PROSE — the tool never ran. They are a runtime REFUSAL recorded as a tool failure, the same conflation as 5.5's suspensions, 5.4's owed arguments and 5.7's breakers. Typing the outcome is what separates them.

output_contract.shape: SUSPENDS — the call returns no result; the turn resumes with an `outcome` of `applied_saved` | `applied_conflict` | `applied_error` | `dismissed`
output_contract._KNOWN_GAP: 🔴 NO SUCCESSFUL CALL EXISTS TO VERIFY AGAINST — 0 of 101. The shape above is read from the tool's own description and the resume contract, and is explicitly NOT marked `_verified_against`, because a shape checked against nothing is the lie that looks like a contract. It becomes verifiable the first time this tool succeeds.
output_contract.closes_when: one recorded `applied_saved` resume exists; the shape is then confirmed or corrected against it.
